fixed_since_v4: The 'I weigh the event' echo is gone: 19/19 in v4, 0/19 now, with no 'weigh ... the event' variant.

No pre-event value is read as the event's outcome (0/19). 11 items label the backdrop 'pre-event' or say it predates the event (33 mentions). The v4 cases (the curve as the cut's verdict, the GDP print as the PMI's effect, 1.75% as the post-cut rate) do not recur.
Velocity is computed as nominal GDP growth minus M2 growth in 19/19 items, and every value is right. It is read correctly in 16/19 (v4: misread in 3, ignored in 1).

The benchmark works as a band. Readings inside it get graded verdicts (m0001 3.7% 'at the floor', m0006 4.5% 'at the top', m0014 3.6% 'inside'). Lagged M2 is used for direction and lags (m0002 'the deceleration is the disinflation'; m0012 explains today's CPI by money growth of 12.3% a year earlier).
The backdrop oil level is no longer treated as a live shock: 7/19 in v4, 0/19 now.

The stock supply-shock argument ('a relative price becomes inflation only if money accommodates') fell from 19/19 to 10/19 by phrase. 5 of those 10 apply it to a real supply or terms-of-trade shock: the coup, drought, strait, blockade and FX items.

Credit SHORT fell from 14/19 to 7/19 (NEUTRAL 10, LONG 2), and 5 of the 7 are tied to the event (PMI, CRE writedown, bank CRE losses, coup, blockade risk). 6 items read wide spreads as already priced; 'little cushion' appears only in m0010.
Probability templating eased. S1 = 0.45 fell from 9/19 to 3/19. Contained events now get base cases of 0.60-0.66 (m0005, m0009, m0015, m0018). Identical scenario labels fell from about 11/19 to 3/19.
All 7 foreign events (m0003, m0007, m0008, m0013, m0015, m0018, m0019) name the foreign variable they lack and never judge the foreign economy with US data.

The episode table now returns Terra, USDC and Reserve Primary, PBoC RRR cuts, and HOLC and HAMP, so m0010, m0017 and m0018 have on-point analogs. m0009, m0014, m0017 and m0019 say where the tool text stops instead of filling the gap from memory.

These v4 per-item errors are fixed: the Plaza money claim (m0005), 'the Fed must tighten' (m0018), velocity in m0011 and m0015, the dollar call against its own chain (m0007), the default credit SHORTs in m0005, m0015, m0018 and m0019, and the equities-SHORT/gold-LONG default in m0019.
Proof refs are bracketed in 19/19, the L5 step cites the modal scenario in 19/19, and one confidence is 'low' (m0018).

remaining_problems: New prompt echoes have replaced 'I weigh': an oil-level disclaimer ('WTI is a level/background, not a live shock; the event is not about energy') in 15/19 items (about 29 occurrences); 'the event states no level, so nothing contradicts the data' in 12/19; 'velocity is not stable / I cannot call velocity stable' in 13/19; and an annualisation remark in 9/19, although only m0011 has a monthly figure. Smaller echoes: 'below any plausible natural rate' in 5, and self-labels or rule references ('a monetarist', 'the monetarist one', 'my supply-shock rule', 'as I always do', 'computed, not assumed') in 7.

About 12 items treat the 4-quarter real growth average as 'trend real growth'. 5 of them move the money benchmark with the cycle (m0001, m0009, m0011, m0015, m0019), which is pro-cyclical and not a constant-growth rule. Arithmetic slips follow: m0001 calls an implied 2.6% inflation a 'deflationary bias'; m0009 says 0.9 + 2 justifies 'even less than 2%'; m0005 calls 2.8 + 2 the 3.5-4.5% band; m0012 says '3.7 above the top' when the gap is 4.3.

Signals follow the backdrop money level, not the event. Gold is LONG in 11/12 items with M2 above the band and NEUTRAL in 6/7 at or below it, and never SHORT. Bonds are LONG in 6/7 items at or below the band and never LONG above it, except m0010's wrong-signed call. About 30 of 114 signal lines in 16/19 items are tagged 'data-driven': the rule capping such calls at conviction 2 is being used as a licence for them. In m0007, m0011 and m0015, pre-event data cancel the event's own tilt.

Money demand and velocity concepts are misused. A rate cut's lower opportunity cost of money is said to release balances into spending (m0000, m0002). Falling velocity 'masks' a money slowdown (m0001). QE1 and 2020 are called responses to 'a collapse in money demand' (m0007). Rising velocity is called the condition for a one-off level shift (m0009). Unemployment below the natural rate is called 'not a source of wage pressure' (m0006).

The supply-shock argument is still applied to non-supply events: a credit default (m0003), a CRE writedown with a self-contradicting Proof L3 (m0004, as in v4), bank CRE losses (m0006) and a fiscal shutdown (m0015). m0019 routes a foreign tariff through US money, and m0001 keeps a token supply-shock scenario.

Claims about money or inflation in past episodes still come from memory, and several are wrong. m0012 and m0013 say the 2021 Ever Given period had 'no lasting change in the money stock' or 'no money-driven inflation' (M2 ~+25%, CPI rising to 7%). m0001 calls Lehman a money contraction, m0004 speaks of Japan's 'collapse in the money stock', m0006 says US money growth fell in 2006-08, and m0003 calls China's 2008 stimulus property relief. The episode table still carries no money context.

Three v4 item errors survive: forced T-bill sales as a bid for bills (m0010), a 0.3pp monthly unemployment rise as survey noise (m0011), and tariff incidence routed through US money (m0019). Two items misread what the pre-event 2y prices: m0002 says the front end is priced when the 2y equals the policy rate, and m0003 says the 2y prices easing when it sits above the policy rate.

Calibration is templated in a new form. S1 is the modal scenario in 19/19 (v4: 17/19), and the modal probability is 0.42-0.55 in 15/19. Three tuples repeat across 6 items: (0.42, 0.33, 0.25), (0.55, 0.25, 0.20) and (0.50, 0.30, 0.20). The v4 tuple (0.45, 0.30, 0.25) appears once more. 'Confidence: moderate' is used in 18/19, and the one 'low' (m0018) sits on a 0.62 modal. The modal scenario contradicts the item's own analogs or chain in m0011, m0012 and m0018.
11/19 Proofs exceed 7 lines, and 5 exceed 8 (m0003 has 10). The pilot-v5 validator accepts up to 10 steps (proof_problems(..., max_steps=10) in collect_v4), not the prompt's 7 or the docstring's 8.

The templates v4 flagged are unchanged. T05-04 names no commodity (m0008 assumes oil). T01-04 gives 500bn with no currency or period (m0007 assumes it is small). T02-06 puts a US-style shutdown in an Asian economy (m0015 turns it into factory idling). Some foreign-event scenarios still do not say whose growth or inflation they describe (m0015, m0019).

The backdrop generator draws M2 as CPI + U(-4, 8). That puts M2 above the band in 12/19 items and makes implied velocity negative in 13/19 (as low as -8.6%). So 'excess money held as idle balances, a latent overhang' recurs across most items and drives the backdrop-keyed gold and bond calls.
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: Delete the sentences that are now echoed rather than adding rules. (a) Drop 'the oil level in the data is not a live shock unless the event concerns energy' and write instead: 'Use an indicator only where your chain needs it; never write a sentence about why an indicator does not matter.' (b) Change the contradiction rule to: 'If the event states a level the data contradict, say which you rely on; otherwise write nothing about contradictions.' (c) Make annualisation conditional on the event giving a monthly figure. (d) Replace 'before calling velocity stable' with 'compute implied velocity growth and say what it means for this event.' In the batch report, count these phrases and warn above about 25%. Extend ECHO to 'monetarist' self-labels, 'live shock', 'states no level', 'annualis' and 'computed, not assumed'.

Define trend in the diagnosis: 'Trend real growth is long-run potential, about 2%, and the 3.5-4.5% band is fixed. The 4-quarter average measures the cycle (slack), not the trend; never move the money benchmark with it.'

Make signals marginal effects: 'Each signal is the event's effect against the no-event baseline. The backdrop does not change because of the event: it may scale conviction but never set or cancel a direction. A direction only the backdrop supports is NEUTRAL.' In the batch report, cross-tabulate gold and bond directions against M2 above or below the band, and warn when more than about 80% align (11/12 and 6/7 here).

Add one sentence on money demand: 'A lower interest rate raises money demand and lowers velocity in the short run; money reaches spending when its quantity outruns demand. Falling velocity compounds a money slowdown and rising velocity offsets it; in a crisis money demand rises; unemployment below the natural rate adds wage pressure.'

Add category hints where the stock argument still leaks or v4 errors persist. Banking, housing, credit defaults and fiscal events: 'ask whether deposits and credit (money) contract; do not use the accommodation argument.' Labour: 'a monthly unemployment change of 0.2pp or more is statistically significant.' Money-market and stablecoin runs: 'forced T-bill sales raise bill yields; a flight to safety lowers them.' Tariffs: 'the price effect lands in the economy that levies the tariff; for the US a foreign tariff means lost exports, and US money cannot accommodate a foreign price level.'

Give the episode table a money-context field (e.g. EP-2021-03-23: US M2 ~+25% y/y; EP-2008-09: US M2 ~+9%; EP-1989-12: Japan M2+CD growth ~10% falling to ~0-2% by 1992; EP-1973-10: US M2 ~+9%; EP-1990-08: US M2 ~+4%), and instruct: 'say nothing about money growth in an episode unless the tool text gives it.'

Scenarios: 'list them in a fixed causal order (for example by growth direction), not by probability', so the modal is not always S1 (19/19 here). Keep v6's Evidence line, and add: 'the modal scenario must be the one your closest analog supports, or say why not' (m0011, m0012, m0018).
Validator: for prompt version 5 and later, set proof_problems max_steps to 7 (11/19 exceed 7, and up to 10 is accepted now).

Templates: name the commodity in T05-04, give currency and period in T01-04 (e.g. '500bn yen a month'), and use 'a budget impasse freezes spending' in T02-06. For foreign events, require scenario labels to name the economy ('US growth', 'Chinese credit').

Backdrop generator: draw M2 around nominal GDP growth (NGDP + U(-3, 3), with occasional larger shocks) so implied velocity centres near zero and a money overhang is not the default backdrop (12/19 above the band and 13/19 with falling velocity here).

Before scaling: keep m0017, m0005, m0014, m0009 (after its arithmetic fix) and m0013 as exemplars. Regenerate m0010 (T-bill sign), m0011 (0.3pp premise), m0019 (tariff incidence) and m0015 (shutdown read as factory idling). Fix m0001 (velocity, deflationary bias), m0012 (2021 claim, base-case mismatch), m0018 (S1 against its analogs and confidence), m0003 (2y misread, accommodation argument) and m0004 (Proof L3).
